# Wald

> Wald distribution.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var wald = require( '@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald' );
```

#### wald

[Wald][wald-distribution] (inverse Gaussian) distribution.

```javascript
var dist = wald;
// returns {...}
```

The namespace contains the following distribution functions:

<!-- <toc pattern="*+(cdf|pdf|mgf|quantile)*"> -->

<div class="namespace-toc">

-   <span class="signature">[`cdf( x, mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/cdf]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution cumulative distribution function.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`logcdf( x, mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/logcdf]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">evaluate the natural logarithm of the cumulative distribution function (CDF) for a Wald distribution.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`logpdf( x, mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/logpdf]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">evaluate the natural logarithm of the probability density function (PDF) for a Wald distribution.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`mgf( t, mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/mgf]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution moment-generating function (MGF).</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`pdf( x, mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/pdf]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution probability density function (PDF).</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`quantile( p, mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/quantile]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution quantile function.</span>

</div>

<!-- </toc> -->

The namespace contains the following functions for calculating distribution properties:

<!-- <toc pattern="*+(kurtosis|mean|mode|skewness|stdev|variance)*"> -->

<div class="namespace-toc">

-   <span class="signature">[`kurtosis( mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/kurtosis]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution excess kurtosis.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`mean( mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/mean]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution expected value.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`mode( mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/mode]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution mode.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`skewness( mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/skewness]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution skewness.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`stdev( mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/stdev]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution standard deviation.</span>
-   <span class="signature">[`variance( mu, lambda )`][@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald/variance]</span><span class="delimiter">: </span><span class="description">Wald distribution variance.</span>

</div>

<!-- </toc> -->

```javascript
var wald = require( '@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald' );

var y = wald.pdf( 2.0, 2.0, 4.0 );
// returns ~0.282
```

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var wald = require( '@stdlib/stats/base/dists/wald' );

/*
A support team is modeling how long it takes agents to resolve tickets. The Wald (inverse Gaussian) distribution is a natural fit for "time until completion" data, as it models the first time a drift-diffusion process crosses a fixed threshold.

Assuming the team has collected the following data:

-      Mean resolution time (μ/mu): 20 minutes.
-      Shape parameter (λ/lambda): 50.0 (controls the spread/skew of resolution times).

We can model resolution times using a Wald distribution with μ (mu) = 20.0 minutes and λ (lambda) = 50.0.
*/

var mu = 20.0;
var lambda = 50.0;

// Output the shape parameter of the resolution times:
console.log( lambda );
// => 50.0

// Adjust distribution parameters to reflect a team handling more variable tickets:
lambda = 60.0;

// Adjusted shape parameter:
console.log( lambda );
// => 60.0

// Excess kurtosis of a Wald distribution (measure of "tailedness"):
console.log( wald.kurtosis( mu, lambda ) );
// => 5.0

// Variance of the resolution times after adjusting lambda:
console.log( wald.variance( mu, lambda ) );
// => ~133.333

// Probability density function at 20 minutes:
console.log( wald.pdf( 20.0, mu, 60.0 ) );
// => ~0.0345

// Cumulative distribution function at 20 minutes (portion of tickets resolved within 20 minutes):
console.log( wald.cdf( 20.0, mu, 60.0 ) );
// => ~0.607

// 50th percentile (median-like) resolution time:
console.log( wald.quantile( 0.5, mu, 60.0 ) );
// => ~17.193

// Moment-generating function value at 0.01 (used in probability theory):
console.log( wald.mgf( 0.01, mu, 60.0 ) );
// => ~1.23

// Mean resolution time:
console.log( wald.mean( mu, 60.0 ) );
// => 20.0

// Mode of the resolution times (most frequent value):
console.log( wald.mode( mu, 60.0 ) );
// => ~12.361

// Variance of the resolution times:
console.log( wald.variance( mu, 60.0 ) );
// => ~133.333

// Skewness of the distribution (symmetry measure):
console.log( wald.skewness( mu, 60.0 ) );
// => ~1.732

var myquantile = wald.quantile.factory( mu, 60.0 );

// 20th percentile (value below which 20% of resolution times fall):
console.log( myquantile( 0.2 ) );
// => ~10.875

// 80th percentile (value below which 80% of resolution times fall):
console.log( myquantile( 0.8 ) );
// => ~27.434

var mylogpdf = wald.logpdf.factory( mu, 60.0 );

// Logarithm of the probability density function at 20 minutes:
console.log( mylogpdf( 20.0 ) );
// => ~-3.365

// Logarithm of the probability density function at 15 minutes:
console.log( mylogpdf( 15.0 ) );
// => ~-3.059
```

</section>
